items.text: The bug fix adds no regression test to guard the race fix, violating the repo's documented standard (contribute/create-pull-request.md:28) that requires bug-fix PRs to include tests that replicate the fixed bug
The dead CDN branch (unreachable due to cdn := "") would hold the exclusive lock across an HTTP call if it were reachable.

Double-checked locking pattern is missing the second check after upgrading from RLock to Lock - after releasing RLock and acquiring Lock, another goroutine may have already populated the cache, but the code proceeds to reload assets from disk without checking. Add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }` after acquiring the write lock to avoid redundant file reads on concurrent cold-start requests.

Double-checked locking pattern is incomplete - after acquiring the write lock at line 48, the code does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache was already populated by another goroutine, causing redundant file I/O and cache overwrites when multiple goroutines queue on the write lock during cold start

After acquiring the write lock, the code should re-check entryPointAssetsCache (and cfg.Env) before recomputing, since another goroutine may have populated the cache while this one waited; without that check, a later compute (or error) can overwrite a good cached value
The package-global cache leaks between tests because nothing resets entryPointAssetsCache, so any concurrent test must reset it

In setting.Dev mode, every call skips the cache and holds the exclusive lock during file I/O, causing Index, frontend-settings and recovery-page requests to be served one at a time instead of in parallel

The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.
Docstring coverage is 0.00% which is insufficient - the required threshold is 80.00%, need to write docstrings for functions missing them
The fix extends package-level global state (adds a global mutex beside the global cache) against the documented guidance to avoid globals; the cache also leaks between tests in the package.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

Incomplete double-checked locking: after acquiring the write lock, the code should re-check entryPointAssetsCache before proceeding to fetch. Between RUnlock() and Lock(), another goroutine could have already populated the cache, causing redundant (and potentially expensive) asset fetches.

A failed fetch unconditionally overwrites the cache with nil (entryPointAssetsCache = result on line 73). If the asset read fails, result is nil and this stomps a previously valid cache entry. Guard the assignment so that a nil result does not overwrite an existing good value.

No re-check of entryPointAssetsCache after acquiring the write lock, so concurrent cold-cache misses serialize and each re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json (duplicate file reads on cold start or after failed load).

In Dev mode every call serializes on manifest file I/O since line 45 bypasses the cache; in production a missing/broken manifest causes every request to retry the failed read serially under the exclusive lock.
Add a second cache check under the write lock to avoid redundant rebuilds - a concurrent caller could fill the cache between the initial RUnlock and Lock, re-checking avoids extra IO

The code does not re-check the cache after taking the write lock, causing concurrent callers that saw nil cache to wait in queue and re-read/re-parse assets-manifest.json one by one, potentially making duplicate network fetches when CDN is enabled. Fix: after Lock(), add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`
The data-race fix ships without a regression test; no test calls GetWebAssets concurrently under the race detector. Bug-fix PRs require tests that replicate the fixed bug.

issues.claim: In GetWebAssets, after acquiring the write lock the code does not re-check whether entryPointAssetsCache was already populated by another goroutine. Concurrent cold-cache callers therefore each re-read and re-parse assets-manifest.json redundantly and overwrite the cache.
The fetch result is unconditionally assigned to entryPointAssetsCache, so a failed fetch stores nil and overwrites a previously valid cache entry.

The data-race fix includes no regression test that calls GetWebAssets concurrently under the race detector. The repo's contribution guidelines (contribute/create-pull-request.md) require bug-fix PRs to include such tests.

In setting.Dev mode every call bypasses the cache and holds the exclusive lock during manifest file I/O, so requests are serialized. In production, a missing or broken manifest causes every request to retry the failed read serially under the lock.
The CDN branch is unreachable because cdn is set to "", and if it were reachable it would hold the exclusive lock across an HTTP call.
Nothing resets the package-global entryPointAssetsCache, so its state leaks between tests.
The fix adds a package-level global mutex beside the global cache, extending global state against the documented guidance to avoid globals.
Docstring coverage is 0.00%, below the required 80.00% threshold.
